title: That theology in the third sense — scholastic theology — is an aggregate habit from faith and the philosophical disciplines
pass_a_gloss: Article XXVI. It is proved that theology taken in the third way — that is, scholastic theology — is an aggregate habit from faith and the philosophical disciplines. 1. Scholastic theology uses faith's principles and at the same time philosophical middles (logic, metaphysics, ethics) to explain and defend conclusions. 2. Therefore it is not a simple habit, but an aggregate from faith and philosophical habits. By logic it arranges arguments; by metaphysics it explains the terms of being and causes; by ethics the virtues and vices of the Decalogue.
pass_b_english: Article XXVI. That theology in the third sense — scholastic theology — is an aggregate habit from faith and the philosophical disciplines.
1. Scholastic theology uses faith's principles together with philosophical middles — logic, metaphysics, ethics — to explain and defend conclusions.
2. So it is not a simple habit but an aggregate of faith and philosophical habits: logic for arguments, metaphysics for being and causes, ethics for the Decalogue's virtues and vices.
source_text:
ART. XXVI.
Probatur Theologiam tertio modo acceptam, hoc est, Theologiam Scholasticam esse habitum aggregatum ex Fide, & Philosophicis disciplinis.

1. Theologia Scholastica utitur principiis fidei & simul mediis philosophicis (logica, metaphysica, ethica) ad conclusiones explicandas & defendendas.

2. Ideo non est habitus simplex, sed aggregatum ex fide & habitibus philosophicis. Beneficio Logicae disponit argumenta; Metaphysicae explicat terminos entis & causarum; Ethicae virtutes & vitia decalogi.
